title: Efficient Continuous Logic Optimization with Diffusion Model
problem: Logic synthesis optimization flows require exhaustive search over exponentially large transformation sequences to improve quality of results (QoR). Existing Bayesian optimization and reinforcement learning methods struggle with efficiency due to the discrete, combinatorial nature of the problem.
motivation: Logic synthesis QoR directly impacts chip area, delay, and power; automating this optimization with better efficiency would enable faster design iterations and better final designs.
method: The approach optimizes synthesis sequences in a continuous latent space by leveraging a diffusion model to map between continuous points and feasible transformation sequences. Gradient information is extracted from a learned QoR surrogate model (trained to predict area/delay), enabling efficient gradient-based optimization while the diffusion model ensures solutions correspond to valid synthesis transformations.
key_novelty: Using diffusion models to bridge the gap between continuous latent space optimization and discrete synthesis transformation feasibility, enabling gradient-based search over normally intractable synthesis sequences.
contributions: A continuous optimization framework for logic synthesis that achieves 5-130x efficiency improvement over Bayesian optimization and RL methods
Integration of a diffusion model to ensure continuous-space solutions map to valid synthesis transformations
Demonstration of lower area and delay on extensive benchmarks compared to prior art

metrics.speedup: 5-130x improvement in efficiency vs. Bayesian optimization and RL

limitations: Evaluation is on logic synthesis benchmarks; scalability to industrial-sized circuits and practical deployment overhead not discussed.
primary_theme: automated synthesis optimization via continuous space
